Thanks Ben — taking point. Hi Ana / Ravi, looping Karthik (Implementation PM) and Marissa (Solutions) so we can map technical scope to rollout milestones.

Initial plan (high level):

1) Discovery & dev access (Days 0-2): confirm API key rotation window, send temporary sandbox keys, and share the sample SDKs.
2) SDK setup & local smoke (Days 3-6): get Node/Python SDKs integrated into their staging service, validate auth, and run basic generation flows.
3) Endpoint migration & canary (Days 7-10): add a feature-flagged route that forwards X% of traffic to Redwood. Observe latency and error rates.
4) Scale & cutover (Days 11-14): increase traffic % with automatic rollback criteria.

Implementation notes:
- SDK initialization (Node example):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({
    apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
    baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1',
    timeoutMs: 60000, // per-request socket+response timeout
  });

- Recommended retries/backoff:
  - Use idempotent request keys for generation retry only on network errors and 5xx.
  - Exponential backoff: base 250ms, factor 2, jitter up to 100ms, max attempts=5.
  - Respect 429 Retry-After header; if absent, apply backoff schedule and circuit-breaker after 30 consecutive 429s.

- Rate limiting guidance:
  - Client should implement a token-bucket at ~200 tokens/sec (aligns to their SLA).
  - For burst handling, allow short bursts up to 4x with smoothing. If server returns 429, apply per-endpoint backoff and lower token rate by 20% for 30s.

- Endpoint migration notes:
  - Map existing POST /api/ai/generate -> POST /v1/generate with identical payload where possible.
  - Preserve conversation state client-side and send short context windows to reduce token usage; we can recommend a rolling-window KV cache later.

I've attached a short implementation checklist and will schedule a kickoff. Karthik / Marissa — can you review the plan and reply with resource/time objections?

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the outline. A few concrete implementation items and timeline adjustments from Eng: 

- We need a staging dataset to validate token usage (seq length distribution). Can BlueCurrent share a small redacted sample (<= 50k tokens) by EOD tomorrow.
- Canary traffic: prefer 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 2 full hours of monitoring at each step. If error rate > 0.7% or p95 latency degrades by >25%, rollback.
- Retry semantics: add a server-side idempotency key header X-Redwood-Idempotency when retrying PUT/PATCH style operations; generation calls should include a client-generated request_id for correlation.
- Timeouts: recommend two-layer timeouts — connection timeout 5s, overall request timeout 60s. For streaming, set initial read timeout 90s but extendable per-chunk.
- Observability hooks: include request_id in logs and sample traces to our console link (see related links). We will add a temporary tag for BlueCurrent in tracing so we can filter.

Planned dates (updated):
- Kickoff meeting: Wed 2027-08-18 09:00 PT (proposed)
- SDK smoke & local validation: Aug 18-20
- Canary cutover window: Aug 21-23
- Full cutover target: Aug 24
